limitations: The study focused on the relationships between a natural environment and components of attitudes, and while environmental perception and behavioral intentions are widely used as indicators of attitudinal loyalty, this methodology can be complemented with objective behavioral measures (e.g., duration of stay, number of visits, number of nature stimuli).

Future research needs to validate the results in other service environments (e.g., retail stores, health facilities, libraries, education institutions) using different sub-samples and from different countries to observe if cultural differences may produce different results.
The influence of different moderators (gender, age, companions, etc.) could be analyzed as literature shows these may influence the assessment of a mall environment.

Results must be cautiously generalized because this study considers a first approach to structural relationships among the proposed variables, in addition to the location of the study in a specific city and with a specific age distribution.
